legacy_client.library: requests (a Session with urllib3 Retry: 3 retries on 429/500/502/503/504, backoff 0.5)
legacy_client.pace: 1 second between requests to one host; timeout 15 seconds
legacy_client.robots: robots.txt of the source's base URL only, never of a feed host; any answer other than 200 with a text type meant no restriction; Disallow lines read for * and coprepancrawler; a TDM heuristic on the file's words
legacy_client.source: legacy repository, src/coprepan/utils/http.py and config/coprepan.yml (read, not changed)

v3_client.pace: at least 10 seconds between requests to one origin, a stated crawl delay as binding minimum, one attempt per request
v3_client.robots: the robots file of every origin that is requested, feed hosts included; 404 means unavailable and allows; 401/403/429 or a challenge on any answer holds the origin for the run

outlets.name: El País
outlets.observed: 403 Forbidden from a Varnish cache for https://feeds.elpais.com/robots.txt; no challenge, no CAPTCHA, no redirect. The item host elpais.com was never asked
outlets.explanation: The legacy crawler read robots.txt of the outlet's base URL (elpais.com) only and treated every non-200 robots answer as no restriction; it never asked for robots.txt of the feed host. v3 asks for the robots file of every origin it requests, and its policy holds an origin whose robots address answers 403. Whether feeds.elpais.com answered 403 for that path in February 2026 is unknown: nobody asked. The feed itself was not requested by v3, so whether it still answers is unknown too
outlets.evidence_limits: one answer per host from one network on one day; nothing is known about other clients or networks
outlets.permitted_solution: a decision whether a 403 for the robots address of a host that only carries feeds is 'robots unavailable' (the reading of RFC 9309 for 4xx) or an access control (the reading of the policy in force, CPD-0017); or an evidenced channel on elpais.com itself (none is known); or the publisher. Not decided and not requested here
